ledger.v2/ is the active ledger. Its latest entry is ledger.v2/9306.yml. The older ledger/ directory holds YAML entries up to 9280 (plus a few special files) and is not where new entries go.

Can I edit a sealed ledger entry to fix a mistake?
No. ledger/ and ledger.v2/ are append-only: a sealed entry is never rewritten. A correction is recorded as a new entry with the next free index that chains to the previous seal.

event_hash uses EVENT_DOMAIN_LEDGER (GARDEN.EVENT.v1.LEDGER) when entry_index >= REGIME_B_FROM, which is 9281; earlier Regime B entries use GARDEN.EVENT.v1. The event is stripped and must be ASCII; Unicode b² is rejected.

How does hexstrike compute a seal?

compute_seal(payload) = sha3_256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)) with default separators, UTF-8 encoded, as a hex digest. This is a different formula from the Regime B event hash in verify_ledger.py.

What finding kinds does hexstrike report?

Four ghost_seal subtypes: forged_seal (declared seal != recomputed seal over payload), empty_payload (seal asserted, payload absent), no_evidence (seal present, evidence_at_seal_time is an empty list), unsealed_with_evidence (evidence present, seal null or absent).

What happens if hexstrike runs under python -I without PyYAML?

Every YAML entry fails with yaml_unavailable, so hexstrike prints INCOMPLETE SCAN, says how many entries could not be parsed, and exits 2 instead of reporting a pass. On main that is 1038 of 1038 entries. No ghost-pass.

Can the known-unparsed list excuse a missing PyYAML?
No. Only parse_error and not_a_mapping failures can be excused by the --known-unparsed list. yaml_unavailable and read errors never can, and listed files are still reported as KNOWN-UNPARSED.

What timestamp format must a new ledger entry use?

ISO 8601 date-time with an explicit offset, Z or +HH:MM / -HH:MM, for example 2026-10-30T14:07:00-04:00. It applies to `timestamp` and every key ending in `_at` at any depth, and a new entry must have a `timestamp`.
